2_Introduction: The resulting hybrid SAMs-modified PSC achieve a champion PCE of 25.7676%, with VOC of 1.1853 V, FF of 81.7075%, and JSC of 26.607 mA/cm². The perovskite (Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0) precursor solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.65 mol/L in a mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. The deposition process involved a two-step spin sequence (1000 rpm/5 s and 5500 rpm/30 s) to achieve a controlled film thickness. During the second spin coating step, 150 µL CB was dripped onto the perovskite film at 15 s before ending the program. The perovskite film was obtained by annealing at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The triple-cation perovskite Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0 is engineered with a tailored A-site cation distribution to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor, thereby enhancing phase stability and suppressing halide ion migration, while the precursor formulation in a DMF:DMSO solvent mixture promotes the formation of a PbI2·DMSO intermediate phase for controlled crystallization. The deposition protocol, employing a two-step spin-coating sequence followed by chlorobenzene antisolvent dripping at a critical 15-second mark, precisely triggers rapid nucleation and governs the growth of densely packed, large grains, with subsequent annealing at 110 °C completing the transformation to a phase-pure, low-stress α-phase perovskite film. The integration of hybrid self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) at the interface provides a multifaceted passivation and energy-alignment strategy, where, for instance, a phosphonic acid-anchored SAM (SAM1) effectively passivates undercoordinated Pb2+ defects through its strong chelating group and introduces a molecular dipole to favorably upshift the perovskite work function, while a complementary carboxylic acid-based SAM (SAM2) targets iodide vacancies and modulates surface energetics. The synergistic interaction between these SAMs arises from their orthogonal passivation mechanisms—SAM1 binding to metal sites and SAM2 to halide sites—which collectively suppress both cationic and anionic defect states, while their combined dipole moments create a graded interfacial energy landscape that facilitates hole extraction and blocks electron recombination. This collective action of the SAM blend, working in concert with the optimized crystallization dynamics from the antisolvent process, results in a perovskite film with superior interfacial quality, minimized non-radiative recombination losses, and enhanced charge carrier selectivity, ultimately yielding a champion solar cell with a power conversion efficiency of 25.7676%, an open-circuit voltage of 1.1853 V, a fill factor of 81.7075%, and a short-circuit current density of 26.607 mA/cm².
